bib.title: Platypus: Quick, Cheap, and Powerful Refinement of LLMs
bib.venue: Workshop on Instruction Tuning and Instruction Following at NeurIPS 2023

question: Can a small, curated, STEM and logic focused instruction dataset plus LoRA fine-tuning and merging of LoRA modules produce top open LLMs cheaply, without test-set contamination?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning on a small high-quality domain dataset conserves the pretrained prior and, combined with merging, improves performance at low cost (building on LIMA's superficial alignment hypothesis).
contributions: Open-Platypus, a small curated dataset of 11 open datasets for STEM and logic
Similarity exclusion process to reduce dataset size and redundancy
Detailed look at test-set contamination and a filtering process
Selection and merging process for specialised LoRA modules

method.summary: LLaMA-2 13B and 70B are LoRA fine-tuned on Open-Platypus in Alpaca format, then the adapters are merged into other fine-tuned LLaMA-2 models (Camel, StableBeluga, Dolphin, instruct) via the PEFT library. Evaluated on the HF Open LLM Leaderboard.
method.task: instruction tuning (SFT, LoRA) and model merging

datasets.name: Open-Platypus
datasets.source: Curated from 11 open datasets: PRM800K, MATH, ScienceQA, SciBench, ReClor, TheoremQA, leetcode-solutions-python-testgen-gpt4, airoboros-gpt4-1.4.1 (keyword-filtered), tigerbot-kaggle-leetcodesolutions-en-2k, ARB, Openassistant-guanaco (keyword-filtered); non-commercial licence due to training set
datasets.preprocessing: Alpaca format; exact dedupe then 80% cosine dedupe keeping longer answer; >80% similarity to test questions removed after manual triage; ARB/ReClor get '{Choose A, B, C, or D}' as input; ScienceQA long-form answers without explicit choice

models.name: Merge partners: Camel, StableBeluga, Llama-2-70b-instruct-v2, Dolphin

other.note: 'base model' = model onto which LoRA adapters are merged

training.objective: supervised instruction tuning, loss not on inputs (train on inputs False)

other.lora_target_modules: gate_proj, down_proj, up_proj (earlier attempts used q/k/v/o_proj)
other.lr_note: 70B lr lowered from 4e-4 to 3e-4 because loss went to zero after 15 steps

inference.prompting: Alpaca template; leaderboard shots: ARC 25, HellaSwag 10, MMLU 5, TruthfulQA 0

parameters.merge_method: PEFT built-in merge of LoRA adapter into base model; merge weights not stated

metrics.name: ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, MMLU, TruthfulQA accuracy and mean
metrics.definition: HF Open LLM Leaderboard average of four benchmarks

baselines: Open LLM leaderboard models (Llama-2-70b-instruct-v2, StableBeluga2, etc.)
eval.protocol: Single leaderboard run, no seeds or significance tests; Camel-Platypus2-70B evaluated locally (leaderboard pending)

prompts.text:
Below is an instruction that describes a task. Write a response that appropriately completes the request.
### Instruction:
{instruction}
### Response:

evidence.quote: we had to lower the initial learning rate for the 70B model from 4e-4 to 3e-4 because the loss went to zero after 15 steps

results.claim: Platypus2-70B-instruct ranked first on the HF Open LLM Leaderboard with average 73.13.
results.setup: LLaMA-2-70B + Open-Platypus LoRA merged with Llama-2-70b-instruct-v2; leaderboard 8/10/23; ARC 25-shot, HellaSwag 10-shot, MMLU 5-shot, TruthfulQA 0-shot
results.quote: securing the top position with an average score of 73.13

results.claim: Stable-Platypus2-13B was the top 13B open model with average 63.96.
results.setup: LLaMA-2-13B Platypus LoRA merged with StableBeluga-13B; leaderboard 8/10/23
results.quote: stands out as the premier 13 billion parameter model with an average score of 63.96

results.claim: A 13B Platypus model trains on a single A100 GPU using 25k questions in 5 hours.
results.quote: our 13B model was fine-tuned using 1 A100 80GB for 5 hours and our 70B model using 4 A100s 80GB for 22 hours

results.claim: Alpaca-7B full fine-tune comparison point: 3 hours on 8 A100s 80GB (Stanford figure).
results.quote: Stanford notes that their full fine-tune of Alpaca-7B took 3 hours on 8 A100s 80GB

results.claim: Only about 10% of Open-Platypus questions are LLM-generated; it comprises 11 open datasets.
results.quote: It is comprised mainly of human-designed questions, with ∼10% of questions generated by an LLM

results.claim: Dedup threshold: remove instructions with 80% cosine similarity (SentenceTransformers) after exact-duplicate removal, keeping the more verbose answer.
results.quote: followed by removal of instructions which had 80% cosine similarity with the SentenceTransformers [30] embeddings of other instructions in our train set

results.claim: Leaked (duplicate) test questions found in training sources: 77 in PRM800K and 77 in MATH, 13 each in airoboros and Openassistant-guanaco, 71 in SciQ (not included).
results.setup: Questions with >80% similarity to benchmark test questions, manually judged; only exact-copy category counts as true leak
results.quote: Duplicate contamination is the only category we count as "true" contamination and corresponds to the number of leaked questions listed in Table 1.
results.table: Table 1, column # Leaked Questions (PRM800K 77, MATH 77, SciQ 71, airoboros 13, Openassistant-guanaco 13, others 0)

results.claim: Merging Platypus with StableBeluga-13B gave +2.91 points on TruthfulQA over the base model.
results.setup: 13B merge, change in percent points vs base (Table 5)
results.quote: with a notable 2.91% increase in TruthfulQA

results.claim: Stable-Platypus2-13B overall increase of +1.05% over base model.
results.quote: Stable-Platypus2-13B also showed an overall increase of +1.05% jump over base model

results.claim: Camel-Platypus2-70B had the largest ARC-challenge gain, +4.12 percent change (+2.82 points).
results.note: Table 5 gives +2.82 as absolute change in percent
results.quote: Camel-Platypus2-70B model exhibited the most significant positive change with a +4.12% improvement in ARC-challenge

results.claim: Dolphin-Platypus2-70B was the only merge that did not beat both base and adapter models.
results.note: Quote may span line break in text; see check

results.claim: Merging effects are domain-specific: MMLU machine_learning +26.32% (Camel-P2-70B) versus abstract_algebra -15.62% (Camel-P2-13B).
results.table: Table 6, row machine_learning, column C-P2-70 (+26.32); row abstract_algebra, column C-P2-13 (-15.62)

results.claim: Platypus2-70B (no merge) ranked 15th with average 70.06; Platypus2-13B ranked 20th among 13B models with 61.35.
results.table: Table 2, row 15. Platypus2-70B, column Avg. (70.06); Table 3, row 20. Platypus2-13B, column Avg. (61.35)

limits: Inherits LLaMA-2 limitations: static knowledge, English-focused, may produce harmful or non-factual content
Keyword search and embedding cosine similarity may not exhaustively catch contamination; merge partners trained on closed datasets cannot be verified
PRM800K includes MATH train and test; used with similar questions removed
No ablation isolating dataset size, dataset content or LoRA versus merging; single run, no seeds
Merge gains are inconsistent: 70B merges vary marginally, Dolphin merge hurt
Claim that merging broadens knowledge not reasoning is inferred from TruthfulQA only
Leaderboard rankings are dated 8/10/23 and obsolete; non-commercial licence

terms.definition: questions that are not exact duplicates and fall within general knowledge, e.g. synonymous answers
